about: Ground-truth activity records and the method each should produce. These are the measuring stick for the whole pipeline: today they test hand-authored tables, and when M2/M3 derive tables from the documents, the SAME cases decide whether the derived rules behave like the authored ones.
circularity_warning: A case is only a real test if its expectation was decided independently of assets/decision-tables.js. Every case therefore carries a `basis`. basis="cited" means the expectation comes from a passage in the corpus, and the citation is recorded. basis="judgement" means it comes from domain reasoning and is weaker evidence. A case whose expectation was read off our own table would prove nothing and does not belong here.

tests_key.selection: the right method is chosen when one clearly applies
tests_key.ordering: the right method wins when SEVERAL could apply - this is what breaks if a derived table gets priority wrong
tests_key.refusal: the engine declines rather than guessing
tests_key.validation: a malformed record is stopped before rule matching

cases.name: Downstream freight, carrier fuel receipt only
cases.why: Fuel consumed is measured activity data. The Corporate Standard p.44 puts metered fuel purchase ahead of proxies.

cases.name: Downstream freight with BOTH fuel and vehicle distance
cases.why: Both qualify. Measured fuel outranks a vehicle-km average because it is primary data for the actual movement.

cases.name: Inbound freight with weight, distance AND spend
cases.why: Tonne-kilometre is the reference method for freight; spend is a screening proxy and must not win when mass and distance exist.
cases.cite: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Technical Guidance (2013), Category 4

cases.name: Purchased goods with a supplier footprint AND an invoice value
cases.why: The guidance ranks supplier-specific first and spend-based last, applying spend only when the others are not feasible.
cases.cite: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Technical Guidance (2013) p.33, Category 1

cases.name: Purchased goods, nothing but an invoice
cases.why: With no supplier data and no mass, the guidance directs the spend-based method against EEIO factors.
cases.cite: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Technical Guidance (2013) p.33, Category 1

cases.name: Air travel with itinerary distance
cases.why: Scope 3 is calculated from activity data such as passenger miles.

cases.name: Business travel with BOTH itinerary distance and expense claim
cases.why: Monetary proxies rank below measured activity data.

cases.name: Site boiler, metered natural gas
cases.why: Scope 1 is calculated from purchased quantities of commercial fuels using published factors.

cases.name: Owned fleet with BOTH fuel card and odometer
cases.why: For owned assets the fuel record is the direct measurement; odometer distance is a derived estimate.

cases.name: Metered grid electricity, no certificates
cases.why: Scope 2 from metered consumption against the local grid factor.

cases.name: Electricity backed by I-REC, no grid region recorded
cases.why: A contractual instrument is evidenced, so the market-based method applies.

cases.name: Electricity with BOTH grid region and I-REC
cases.why: RECORDED AS A KNOWN DEFECT, NOT AS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR. Scope 2 Guidance section 7.4 requires dual reporting - BOTH figures. A first-match engine can only return one. The expectation records what the engine does today so the gap stays visible and measurable; it must change when the engine learns multi_applicable.
cases.cite: GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance (2015) section 7.4 Dual reporting

cases.name: Waste with weighbridge ticket naming stream and route
cases.why: Stream and treatment route are both known, which is the most specific waste basis available.

cases.name: Refrigerant with BOTH a recharge log and nameplate charge
cases.why: Gas actually added is observed; a leak-rate screen is an assumption. Mass balance outranks screening.

cases.name: Employee commuting from a survey
cases.why: Surveyed distance by mode is more specific than a national per-employee average.

cases.name: Investment where the investee reports AND value is known
cases.why: Reported investee emissions allocated by share is primary data; economic allocation is a proxy.

cases.name: Business travel record with context only
cases.why: Nothing measurable was supplied. The standard requires the most accurate approach AVAILABLE; it never authorises a default when none applies.

cases.name: Fuel quantity entered as zero
cases.why: A zero quantity is not an activity. Treating it as present would produce a spurious zero-emission result rather than a data gap.

cases.name: Distance given with no unit
cases.why: A bare number is uninterpretable. Guessing the unit is exactly the silent default the design forbids.

cases.name: Negative energy consumption
cases.why: Activity data cannot be below zero.

cases.name: Reporting year outside the open window
cases.why: A closed inventory year should be rejected rather than silently recalculated.
